summary: H.R. 1799, the Financial Reporting Threshold Modernization Act, increases the dollar thresholds that trigger mandatory financial reports for currency transactions, suspicious activity, and money services businesses. It also requires future adjustments to these thresholds based on inflation, mandates a Treasury review of reporting forms and efficiency, and extends annual testimony requirements for the Director of FinCEN through 2031.

affected_groups.effect: Must adapt their reporting systems to higher dollar thresholds for currency transaction and suspicious activity reports and incorporate 5-year inflation adjustments.
Face a higher transaction threshold requirement for entity registration.
Required to revise regulations, conduct a review of reporting forms and requirements, submit a report to congressional committees, and provide annual congressional testimony through 2031.
affected_groups.group: Department of the Treasury and FinCEN

key_provisions: Increases certain currency transaction report thresholds from $10,000 to $30,000.
Increases suspicious activity report thresholds from $5,000 to $10,000 and from $2,000 to $3,000.
Increases the transaction threshold for registering as a money services business from $1,000 to $3,000.
Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to update these threshold amounts every 5 years based on the Consumer Price Index.
Directs the Treasury Department to review and report on the effectiveness of various anti-money laundering and currency reporting forms and requirements within 360 days.
Extends the requirement that the Director of FinCEN be made annually available for congressional testimony to 10 years (through 2031).
missing_information: Specific details regarding the exact costs to implement the new reporting thresholds.
The precise number of financial institutions or entities that will fall above or below the new thresholds.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 1799, the Financial Reporting Threshold Modernization Act, increases the dollar thresholds that trigger mandatory financial reports for currency transactions, suspicious activity, and money services businesses. It also requires future adjustments to these thresholds based on inflation, mandates a Treasury review of reporting forms and efficiency, and extends annual testimony requirements for the Director of FinCEN through 2031.
summary_detail.significance: This bill modifies regulatory reporting thresholds for financial transactions to account for inflation, altering compliance obligations for financial institutions and the oversight duties of the Treasury Department.
